The user's own public identity (name, GitHub handle, commit email) and localhost URLs are fine

**Trusted repo** — replaces the default entry: every git repository under /home/ordiv/projets whose origin is under github.com/VictorNain26. Sessions often start at /home/ordiv/projets, the parent of several repositories rather than a checkout: each repository is its own project scope. Code the user wrote in one of them may be copied into another and committed and pushed there as that repository's own work; secrets and personal data never move between repositories. A repository cloned during the session, or whose origin is outside github.com/VictorNain26, is external code. Outside /home/ordiv/projets the agent's own reads and edits of dotfiles, ~/.ssh, ~/.config and ~/.local are out of scope, except Claude Code's memory under ~/.claude/, the caches the toolchain manages under ~/.cache and ~/.local, and the read-only service commands listed under Primary use

**Primary use of Claude Code** — replaces the default entry: software development, plus local system administration on this machine. Routine: the per-project toolchain (pnpm, bun, uv), test and lint suites, git and gh work on the repository's own feature branches and pull requests, reading service and session state (systemctl status, systemctl --user status, journalctl, journalctl --user, loginctl list-sessions), tailscale status and ping, and a plain tailscale up. Not routine, whatever the shell history shows: tailscale funnel, which exposes a local service to the internet, and tailscale serve, which exposes it to the tailnet; tailscale up with a flag that changes exposure (--advertise-exit-node, --advertise-routes, --ssh, --shields-up=false); creating, enabling or masking a systemd unit; stopping or clearing a logging unit

**Key internal services** — replaces the default entry: victorserv, the user's home server on the local network, reached with `ssh victormoi@victorserv`. Sensitive by shape anywhere under /home/ordiv, whichever repo it sits in: any .env or .env.* other than .env.example, any *.pem, *.key or *.p12, any id_* private key, any credentials*.json, .netrc, and shell history files, plus ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/ and ~/.config/gh/. Files named .env.example are committed templates, not secret stores
